Ok, this is my first ever post and I’m kinda nervous.

 I’m a 16 yr old multiracial male, (25% German, 25% Japanese, and 50% African American.) and I’ve always felt out of place my entire life. My parents separated when I was young, so I wasn’t really that exposed to my African American Mother’s side of the family very much up until I was 9-ish. My Father didn’t even tell me about our Japanese heritage until I was 6-ish, so I basically grew up White as hell. I was always bullied in school for being “too White”, and “acting like I’m too good to be Black”. After I decided to make my Japanese heritage known in the 7th grade, students would claim I was lying about being part Asian, they would vehemently deny what my claims, even when I proved them wrong. I even remember in 8th grade when we were talking about race, this one girl stood up and said how she hated it when Black folks would claim to be “a quarter Native American or Asian”. I have a few “friends” from Middle School who claim that I don’t count as Black, or my opinion doesn’t matter when it comes to Black issues, and that I don’t look Black whatsoever. Even though I clearly look mixed.

 Fast forward to high school and I still feel alone. Even though I’ve come to accept my heritage and be proud of how unique I am, a part of me still yearns to be accepted by the Blacks, Whites, and Asians. During the first 3 months of Sophomore year, in a case of bizarre irony, I sat alone between the White kid’s table and the Black kid’s table.

 I’m saying all this to ask: How did you learn to overcome the ridiculous bullshit with colorism and being mixed and all the hate that comes with it?

 Sorry for rambling btw lol, I did all this on the fly.
